title: Enrollment in N.Y.C. Schools Falls by 23,000
summary: New York City has lost 200,000 students over the past decade, mirroring declines in districts across the United States.

Enrollment in New York City’s public school system has fallen by 23,000 students from last school year, the city’s Department of Education said on Monday, deepening a multiyear slide that has steadily shrunk and reshaped the country’s largest school district.


There are now 766,900 students in kindergarten through 12th grade, a nearly 3 percent decline from the previous year and the largest year-over-year decrease in five years. During the past decade, the city’s schools have lost 200,000 students.


The steep decline started before the coronavirus pandemic, accelerated in its early years and then briefly stabilized amid an influx of migrant families. Now it is deepening once again, driven by declining birthrates and families leaving the city, another example of the affordability crisis that Mayor Zohran Mamdani has staked his administration on addressing.


To confront the growing number of schools with dwindling enrollment, school leaders have suggested some closures, but just a few so far.


“We are facing generational shifts in birthrates and out-migration that can’t be ignored,” Kamar Samuels, the city’s school chancellor, said. “I’m committed to ensuring our school system faces the issue of declining enrollment head on by redoubling our efforts to build the rigorous, supportive schools New Yorkers want for their children.”


School districts[across the country have been losing students for years](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/08/upshot/public-schools-enrollment-crisis.html) , a trend fueled by a two-decade decline in the United States in fertility rates, which hit[a record low in 2025](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/09/us/fertility-rates-decline.html) . The prolonged contraction has upended public education nationwide, leaving behind half-empty schools and forcing painful budget cuts.
